newsitem.title: USA: Clinton declines comment on McVeigh verdict.
newsitem.headline: Clinton declines comment on McVeigh verdict.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday said the end of Timothy McVeigh's trial represented a "long overdue day" for the survivors and families of those who died in the Oklahoma City bombing.

Clinton, in a written statement, declined to comment on the verdict in which McVeigh was found guilty on all counts in the bombing of a federal building in Oklahoma City on April 19, 1995, which killed 168 people.

"I cannot comment on the jury's verdict. But I will say that this is a very important and long overdue day for the survivors and families of those who died in Oklahoma City," he said of the Denver trial.

Clinton was constrained from discussing the verdict because the jury had to decide McVeigh's sentence and a second defendant in the bombing, Terry Nichols, is to stand trial, and the president wanted to do nothing to prejudice the legal process.
He said he was particularly proud of the work done by Attorney General Janet Reno, the prosecutors, the FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms.

"Two years ago, I spoke to the families of the 168 people who lost their lives at the Murrah federal building," Clinton said. "I told them that though they had lost much, they had not lost everything -- and they had not lost America.

"I pledged then and I pledge now that we will stand with them for as many tomorrows as it takes. Today, I say to the families of the victims, no single verdict can bring an end to your anguish. But your courage has been an inspiration to all Americans. Our prayers are with you," he said.
